No drone crashes were reported.

"Das sind bei jedem Mitglied meiner Fraktion schon über 20.000 E-Mails, die eingegangen sind, in allen möglichen Sprachen aus aller Herren Länder mit ganz vielen verschiedenen Absenderadressen. Several Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were hit by a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems, though the company says operations continue and product freshness is assured.
Published: 02.11.26 11:48 , Update: 02.11.26 12:01
Illustrative image
© Delhaize
Several Delhaize supermarkets became the target of a cyberattack on Monday, which specifically affected fridge and freezer units. The majority of impacted stores are in Belgium, with dozens reportedly affected, but a number of Luxembourg branches were also hit.
A Delhaize spokesperson confirmed the incident to RTL, stating that the company took immediate action to ensure stores remained operational and to guarantee the freshness of products.
Delhaize did not specify which Luxembourg locations were affected in its response to RTL.

BRUSSELS — Refrigerators in dozens of supermarkets in at least five EU countries were out of service on Monday, local news outlets reported, in what appears to be a repeat of cyberattacks that hit French stores last month.
As of Monday afternoon, there were news reports of incidents affecting supermarkets in Belgium , Luxembourg , Sweden , Ireland , the Netherlands and Estonia .
Several store managers told local media that refrigerator temperatures suddenly spiked to up to 50 degrees Celsius. This mirrors the French incidents last month, in which attackers appeared to remotely manipulate the fridges’ defrosting mechanisms so that they overheated.

France has opened an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during protests against the rising cost of living in Paris on Saturday.

Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France for a third weekend of demonstrations. Clashes erupted in Paris and other cities, with police reporting attacks involving projectiles and incendiary devices.
Dramatic footage circulating on social media shows a police officer performing crowd-control duties when his leg suddenly catches fire after an explosive device goes off at his feet.

France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on security forces
AFP
Published: 01.11.26 14:23 , Update: 01.11.26 14:25
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said some rioters had displayed an 'extraordinary' level of violence
© AFP
France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.
On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and some other cities after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs. 
The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has decried an "extraordinary" level of violence from some rioters.

Russia’s Justice Ministry has added the Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces at the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) to its list of “undesirable” organizations, a move that renders affiliation with the anti-war group illegal.
The delegation of Russian exiles was set up in January after years of lobbying efforts by leading opposition figures like former businessman Mikhail Khodorkovsky.
Several members of the anti-war group, including dissident Vladimir Kara-Murza and Pussy Riot co-founder Nadya Tolokonnikova, already face criminal prosecution in Russia.
Under Russian law, individuals affiliated with an “undesirable” entity can face up to four years in prison. Organizing the work of an “undesirable” group carries a maximum sentence of six years in prison.

Russian man arrested in Poland on espionage charges after photographing trains
October 30, 2026, 2:42 pm
Source: Rzeczpospolita
Police detained a 55-year-old Russian man in the city of Świdnica, in Poland’s Lower Silesian Voivodeship, after he photographed trains and railway infrastructure, the newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported.
The detention came during a police operation to secure a soccer match. After the game ended, officers patrolling the city noticed a parked car near a railroad crossing. The man inside tried to flee when he spotted the police.
After stopping him, police found professional photography equipment and files showing he had photographed trains and critical railway and transportation infrastructure, not only in Poland.
He has been charged with espionage, and a court ordered him held in custody for three months. Under Polish law, the offense carries a minimum sentence of five years in prison. His name has not been released.

A Russian citizen was charged with espionage in Poland after he was caught taking photographs of the country’s railway infrastructure, police in Lower Silesia said Friday.
Authorities said officers patrolling after a football match in Świdnica, south-western Poland, stumbled upon the 55-year-old Russian national as he was taking photographs of passing trains at an unguarded railway crossing.
“Everything indicates that the photos he took could be used against the security of the state,” the regional police authority wrote in a press release .

Police found a large amount of evidence suggesting that the man took pictures of strategic infrastructure systematically. “There were photographs of various places and important communication facilities, not only in Poland,” Łukasz Dutkowiak, a spokesperson for the Lower Silesian police, told Radio Wrocław .
Prosecutors are now investigating “activities for foreign intelligence against the Republic of Poland,” the regional authority added.

Pentagon urges Baltic NATO allies to tone down rhetoric about Russia, citing remarks likening Putin to a ‘rat in a corner’
October 30, 2026, 8:49 am
Source: Reuters
Pentagon officials urged several NATO member countries to tone down their rhetoric about the Russian threat during bilateral meetings, according to Reuters sources.
The requests went to Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia, among others, the agency’s sources said. It is unclear whether other countries received similar requests.
Elbridge Colby, head of the Pentagon’s policy directorate, was one of the officials who conveyed the requests. He cited public statements by Europeans describing Russia as “cornered like a rat” as an example of inappropriate rhetoric.
It is unclear which statement he meant, but in late September, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal called Putin a “rat in a corner” and suggested that Russia is resorting to sabotage in Europe because it is increasingly bogged down in the war with Ukraine, Reuters said.

Image source, State Emergency Service Of Ukraine
By Tom McArthur
Published
29 October 2026, 12:38 GMT
Updated 1 hour ago
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.
Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.
In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to Ukrzaliznytsia head Oleksandr Pertsovsky. He said many people were on the platform when the Russian drone struck.
"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform," he said.

Russian attacks cause new power outages in three Ukrainian oblasts | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo: Getty Images
As of the morning of 29 October, Russian attacks had caused new power outages in Donetsk, Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts.
Source: Artem Nekrasov , First Deputy Minister of Energy
Details: Energy workers will begin emergency repairs as soon as the security situation allows.
Advertisement:





Meanwhile, emergency power cuts are being implemented in the city of Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast due to equipment damage. Previously published schedules do not apply in areas affected by these emergency cuts.
Due to grid restrictions caused by Russian attacks, some regions are also experiencing scheduled hourly power cuts, while industrial and business consumers face power capacity restrictions.
Background:
The day before, Ukrenergo announced scheduled hourly power cuts for 29 October.
However, on the morning of 29 October, emergency power cuts were introduced in parts of Kyiv's Holosiivskyi and Solomianskyi districts.

Russian forces have attacked the railway station in Dnipro, killing at least 13 people. The number of those injured is not yet known.
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, announced this on Telegram , Ukrinform reports.


"Thirteen people have been killed in the Russian attack on Dnipro," he wrote.


At least five people were also injured. Medical personnel are providing them with the necessary assistance.
